sections.content: Spanish uses a different verb for different kinds of "becoming". *Ponerse* + adjective is a change of mood or state that can pass: Mi amiga se puso muy triste. *Volverse* + adjective is a deeper change: Mi vecino se volvió muy serio. *Hacerse* + noun is a change you reach by effort or with time: Un amigo mío se hizo médico. *Quedarse* + adjective is the result of something: Mi amiga se quedó sola. You also use *convertirse en* + noun and *pasar de ser … a ser …* for bigger changes, and you know *seguir* + gerund from A2 Unit 28.

items.spanish: La ciudad ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años.
items.english: The city has changed a lot in recent years.

items.spanish: La tecnología se ha convertido en una parte importante de la vida diaria.
items.english: Technology has become an important part of daily life.

items.spanish: La situación pasó de ser estable a ser más complicada.
items.english: The situation went from being stable to being more complicated.

items.spanish: Cuando oyó la noticia, mi amiga se puso muy triste.
items.english: When she heard the news, my friend became very sad.

items.spanish: Mi vecino se volvió muy serio después de aquel día.
items.english: My neighbour became very serious after that day.

items.spanish: Un amigo mío se hizo médico.
items.english: A friend of mine became a doctor.

items.spanish: Cuando se fue su familia, mi amiga se quedó sola en casa.
items.english: When her family left, my friend was left alone at home.

sections.content: Choose the verb by the kind of change: *ponerse* and *quedarse* for a state that can pass, *volverse* for a deeper change, *hacerse* for a change you reach by effort or with time.
